feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: Follow NPR National News for reporting across the United States. Explore coverage of economic affordability, immigration, climate, environmental policy, justice and social trends.

entry.title: Blanche defends DOJ lawsuit blocking Alaska Senate results if Republican loses
entry.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the Justice Department's suit over Alaska's Senate race in an interview on CNN.

entry.title: The U.S. is the largest grower of a cereal you've never heard of
entry.summary: The U.S. is the world's leading supplier of sorghum. Sorghum growers are working to introduce it to American diets.

entry.title: In Arkansas, Democrats see an opening at the edge of the competitive midterms map
entry.summary: In a sign of the potentially dire midterm political environment, Republicans have spent millions of dollars playing defense in Arkansas, one of the most conservative states in the country.

entry.title: Archdiocese of New York agrees to $800 million settlement over sexual abuse claims
entry.summary: The 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse by clergy members and lay workers have all agreed to the settlement, according to an attorney for some of the plaintiffs.

entry.title: Texas voters cast early ballots in key senate race
entry.summary: In Texas, early voting is underway. The state's tight race for U.S. Senate will ultimately help decide the balance of power in Washington.

entry.title: Comedian Charlie Berens has made Wisconsin politics a laughing matter
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with comedian and former journalist Charlie Berens. His comedy blends political satire with a distinctly Wisconsin sense of humor.

entry.title: 'Swing State of the Union' podcast digs deep on issues weighing on Wisconsin voters
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Sam Woods and Joy Powers, hosts of WUWM's Swing State of the Union podcast, about the top issues for voters in the swing state of Wisconsin.

entry.title: How data centers became a bipartisan political issue in Wisconsin
entry.summary: Data centers are a big issue across the country. As midterms approach, many look to the swing state of Wisconsin for lessons for how that issue could play out nationally.

entry.title: U.S. birth rate drops to record low, but older women are having more babies
entry.summary: The U.S. birth rate fell to its lowest level ever recorded, according to a report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The drop would have been greater, but women over age 30 are having more children.

entry.title: Flooding in Four Corners region displaces residents, as storms move southeast
entry.summary: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.
